headline: Vaughan home prices are about 5% lower than a year ago, and the Bank of Canada just raised its rate to 2.5%. Few new condos are starting, but Vaughan has cut its own development fees to zero to help builders. Buyers have more room to negotiate than in recent years.

status.label: Fewer new projects starting
status.explanation: Vaughan has 3,144 homes under construction, down from 3,588 a year ago and far below the peak of 9,815. There are 89 active development applications in the VMC area, but none were received in the last 180 days.

status.label: Buyers are holding back
status.explanation: Across the GTA, October home sales were down 7.9% from a year earlier. In Vaughan, 263 homes sold in October and there were about 4.8 months of listings on the market.

status.label: Prices below last year
status.explanation: The typical Vaughan condo apartment was priced at $504,900 in October, down 6.5% from a year ago. The typical home of any type was $1,106,600, down 5.5%.

status.label: Rents flat to softer
status.explanation: Average rent in the wider Richmond Hill/Vaughan/King zone was $1,726 in 2025, down from $1,762 in 2024. CMHC says asking rents in Toronto have been falling as new rental units open. This zone is larger than the VMC.

status.label: Rates up, fees down
status.explanation: The Bank of Canada raised its rate on October 28 and says it may need to raise it again. At the same time, Vaughan and York Region have lowered or delayed development fees, which can help new projects.

personas.bottom_line: Condo prices are lower than a year ago, but borrowing costs just went up.

points.text: The typical Vaughan condo apartment costs $504,900, down 6.5% from a year ago and well below the 2022 peak of $864,400.
The Bank of Canada raised its rate to 2.5% on October 28. The posted 5-year mortgage rate was 6.19% (posted rates are usually higher than rates people actually get).

watch: Next Bank of Canada decision on December 9, 2026

personas.bottom_line: Rents in the wider area are flat to lower, and more rental homes are being built.

points.text: Average rent in the Richmond Hill/Vaughan/King zone was $1,726 in 2025, with a vacancy rate of 2.4%. This zone is bigger than the VMC.
CMHC says Toronto asking rents have fallen as many new condo units were put up for rent.
Rental apartment starts in Toronto have outpaced condo starts, which could add rental choices later.

watch: CMHC's Rental Market Report due in December 2026

personas.bottom_line: Detached homes and townhouses are cheaper than a year ago, but still costly.

points.text: The typical Vaughan detached home was $1,482,000 in October, down 5.4% from a year ago. A typical townhouse was $714,500, down 8.9%.
Higher borrowing costs may limit how much a family can afford to borrow even if prices are lower.
Ontario unemployment was 7.3% in October, up from 7.0% in September, which may make job security a concern for some households.

personas.bottom_line: Sellers face a softer market with more homes for sale and buyers who negotiate.

points.text: Vaughan homes sold at about 97% of list price in October, and there were 1,219 active listings.
The typical Vaughan home price is 30% below its March 2022 peak of $1,587,400.

personas.bottom_line: Falling prices and flat rents mean weaker returns right now, with some upside if rates ease later.

points.text: The rate hike to 2.5% raises borrowing costs. The Bank says it may need to hike again.
Vaughan condo apartment resales: 57 sales in October with 419 active listings, which is a lot of supply for buyers to choose from.
Rents in the wider zone slipped in 2025, and CMHC expects easing to be most visible in Toronto.
Vaughan has set residential city development charges to zero until October 31, 2027, which could help new projects get built.

personas.bottom_line: A lower price on a house may be offset by lower condo prices to move into.

points.text: Detached homes are down 5.4% and condo apartments down 6.5% from a year ago, so both sides of a move have shifted.
About 4.8 months of listings means sales may take longer than they did in 2021-22.
Fewer new condo projects are starting, so choice of new buildings may be limited later.

scenarios.name: base
scenarios.summary: Prices drift sideways to slightly lower while borrowing costs stay elevated. New condo starts stay low, and existing projects continue.

assumptions.assumption: Stays at 2.5% or rises once more to 2.75% by mid-2027, then holds.
Residential city development charges stay at zero until October 31, 2027.
Months of inventory stays between 4 and 6.

drivers.text: Lower regional and city development fees help project costs.

scenarios.name: optimistic
scenarios.summary: Inflation cools, rates stop rising, and buyers return. Prices stabilise and more projects start.

assumptions.assumption: Holds at 2.5% with no further hikes through 2027.
Falls from about 3% toward the Bank's 2% target by mid-2028, as the Bank projects.
Fee cuts at city and regional level lead to more starts than the 1,243 so far in 2026.
GTA new condo sales keep rising from last year, as Urbanation's Q3 headline suggests.

drivers.text: Fee cuts and deferrals lower builders' costs.

scenarios.name: pessimistic
scenarios.summary: More rate hikes, trade trouble and job losses keep buyers away. Prices fall further and more projects stall.

assumptions.assumption: Rises to 3% or more by 2027 if inflation stays high.
New U.S. tariffs slow Canadian growth in late 2026.
Ontario unemployment stays at or above 7%.
Vaughan starts stay below 1,500 units over the next 12 months.

drivers.text: Higher rates and trade risks weigh on demand.

baseline_views.reason: Prices are down 5.5% from a year ago and the Bank of Canada just raised its rate, which adds pressure.
No strong evidence to depart from the baseline; sales are weak but fee cuts help supply.
Condo apartments fell 6.5% over the past year and there are 419 active condo listings; the baseline assumes no change.
The baseline already allows for further decline.
Starts are 1,243 so far in 2026, but city fee cuts may help.
No clear evidence of a change; condo starts are weak across the GTA.
Starts (1,243 in 2026 to date) are below completions (1,733), so the count is likely to keep falling.
CMHC reports falling asking rents and expects vacancy to rise in 2026.

events.title: Bank of Canada raises its rate to 2.5%
events.impact: Its first change in a year. It says inflation is high and it may raise again. Higher rates make mortgages more costly.

events.title: York Region lowers development charges
events.impact: Region-wide residential charges fall 2-9% and high-rise charges can wait until occupancy.

events.title: Vaughan cuts residential city development charges to zero
events.impact: In effect until October 31, 2027. Regional charges still apply.

events.title: Urbanation says GTHA new condo sales doubled from a year ago in Q3
events.impact: Only the headline was seen; sales started from a very low level.

events.title: Ontario unemployment rises to 7.3%
events.impact: Higher unemployment can reduce demand for homes.

watch_list.threshold: December 9, 2026: another hike would push mortgage costs higher
Below 95% would signal buyers have more power; it was 97% in October
watch_list.why: Shows how strong buyers' bargaining is.

watch_list.threshold: Below 2,500 would signal slower building; 3,144 now

watch_list.why: Builders may rush or delay around this date.

watch_list.threshold: Above 3% in the CMHC Dec 2026 report (2.4% in 2025)
watch_list.why: More vacancy would push rents down.
